chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When I was made to ascend to Heaven, Jibril led me to a place where Jibril had never tread before. It was then unveiled for him, and Allah showed him of His Light of Grandeur what He wished.
ai.seo_question: What did Allah show the Prophet during his ascension when Jibril reached a place he had never tread before?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi describes the Prophet's ascension (Isra and Mi'raj), specifically highlighting a unique location reached by Jibril that he had never visited before. In this place, Allah unveiled His presence to the Prophet, showing him a manifestation of His Light of Grandeur (Nur 'Azamatih) according to His will, emphasizing the divine attributes and the reality of seeing God's light. Within Shia theology, this is often cited in the debate on *Ru'ya Allah* (seeing God), with scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi interpreting it as seeing God's light or essence in a manner befitting His majesty, distinct from physical sight, thereby affirming the possibility of vision without limiting God to a form.

en.ammaar-muslim: 4. [4/323] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya and other than him from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abi al-Hasan al-Ridha عليه السلام who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:  When I was made to ascend to Heaven - Jibril led me to a place where Jibril had never tread on. (The Imam says:) It was then unveiled for him (the prophet) and Allah showed him of His Light of Grandeur what He wished.
